questions.q: Where did the man bring Ezekiel?
questions.a: The man brought Ezekiel out to the outer courtyard on the north side.

questions.q: What were the length and width of the chambers on the north side?
questions.a: The chambers were 100 cubits from east to west and 50 cubits from north to south.

questions.q: How wide was the passage in front of the chambers?
questions.a: The passage was ten cubits wide.

questions.q: How did the highest chambers compare with the lower and middle chambers?
questions.a: The highest chambers were shorter than the lower and middle chambers because the ledges took space from them.

questions.q: How many stories did the chambers have?
How long was the wall that ran along the front of the chambers?
How long were the chambers that were along the outer courtyard?
questions.a: The chambers along the outer courtyard were 50 cubits long.

questions.q: Where was the entrance to the chambers?
questions.a: The entrance was on the east side, where a person came in from the outer courtyard.

questions.q: How did the measurements of the southern chambers compare with the northern chambers?
questions.a: The southern chambers were the same as the northern chambers, with the same length, width, exits, and openings.

questions.q: On which side was the entrance to the walkway of the southern chambers?
questions.a: The entrance to the walkway was on the east side.

questions.q: For what did the man say the northern and southern chambers in front of the court were used?
questions.a: The priests who are allowed to approach Yahweh ate the most holy offerings in those chambers, and they also stored the most holy offerings there.

questions.q: What were the most holy offerings that the priests put in the chambers?
questions.a: The most holy offerings were the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering.

questions.q: What did the priests have to do before going out where the rest of the people are allowed?
questions.a: The priests had to leave the clothes in which they ministered in the sacred areas and put on other clothes before going out where the rest of the people are allowed.

questions.q: What did the man do after he finished measuring the inner house?
questions.a: The man brought Ezekiel out through the gate that faced east and measured the area all around the outside.

questions.q: What was the length of each side; north, south east and west?
What two things did the wall around the area separate?
questions.a: The wall separated the holy from the common.

commentary.text: In this chapter are described the priests' chambers, their use, and the dimensions of the holy mount on which the temple stood. These chambers were many. Jesus said, In my Father's house are many mansions: in his house on earth there are many; multitudes, by faith, are lodging in his sanctuary, and yet there is room. These chambers, though private, were near the temple. Our religious services in our chambers, must prepare for public devotions, and further us in improving them, as our opportunities are.
